content:
Maria: Heads-up — CI perf unit flagged a regression on PR 21801, microbench `adaptive_batcher_hotpath` exceeded threshold by +7.3% (threshold +5%).
Maria: ci-bot posted the diff: `median_latency: +7.3% (was 12.1ms -> 13.0ms)`
ci-bot: [ALERT] perf-threshold-failure for pr/21801 on linux-gpu-x86 (job: microbench-adaptive-batcher). See /artifacts/21801/bench-summary.txt
Jon: ugh. that PR touched the batching timer and the kernel route decision.
Sophia: which commit in the PR is the likely culprit? there are 3 authored commits.
Maria: my hunch is the third — it changed `prefer_quant_route` fallback and added a tiny delay to slot aggregation.
Kevin: can we repro locally quickly? i can run the microbench with `--sample-seqlen=64` and a short run.
Devon: i pulled the perf artifacts — attaching flamegraph snippet (excerpt):
```
flamegraph: adaptive_batcher_hotpath > kernel_select > kv_cache_lookup
heavy: kernel_select::choose_route() +40ms
  prefer_quant_route() +24ms
  fallback_path() +12ms
```
Sophia: interesting that `kv_cache_lookup` shows small spike too. could be interaction between slot delay and KV hit pattern.
Jon: if slot aggregation delays even 2ms it can shift batching alignment and cause more expensive kernel to be chosen (higher coldpath).
Maria: i've queued a `git bisect` across the PR branch to narrow to a commit, but bisect needs the CI job to run which is slow. anyone have a faster repro?
Kevin: try toggling `--batch-window-ms=0` vs `--batch-window-ms=4` locally. that mirrors the change.
Devon: running `./microbench --bench adaptive_batcher_hotpath --batch-window-ms=4 --iters=1000` now.
ci-bot: repro instructions: `bazel test //perf:adaptive_batcher_hotpath --runs_per_test=1 --test_arg=--sample_seqlen=64`
Perf-bot: historical baseline (last green): median_latency 12.1ms, p95 28.4ms. Current failing run: median 13.0ms, p95 31.2ms.
Kevin: local run done — i see median 12.0ms with `--batch-window-ms=0`, 13.1ms with `--batch-window-ms=4` (matches CI).
Kevin: flamegraph locally shows `choose_kernel_route` spending more time in quant_fallback for longer sequences.
Sophia: does quant_fallback select a different kernel that causes KV cache eviction pressure?
Devon: i checked kv metrics in the artifact: `kv_hit_rate` drops 2.6% and `kv_evictions/sec` up x1.5 during the hotpath.
Maria: that supports the theory: slightly larger batch alignment -> different kernel selection -> larger KV footprint -> more evictions -> tail latency up.
Jon: okay plan: 1) revert the slot-aggregation delay in the PR branch and re-run CI; 2) add a targeted unit test that asserts kernel selection invariants for sample seqlen distributions; 3) instrument kernel selector to log why it picked fallback.
Sophia: +1. also add a microbench mode that pins kv cache size to remove eviction variance for testing.
Maria: i'm filing a revert PR now to unblock rollout. will include the perf artifact link in the revert description.
Maria: revert PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/21805
Jon: can someone trigger a quick CI run on the revert? if it goes green we merge and then we can iterate.
ci-bot: queued job: `microbench-adaptive-batcher` for pr/21805. ETA ~25m.
Perf-bot: note: if revert lands, we should still follow up to find root cause — maybe kernel cost model brittle to tiny timing shifts.
Kevin: i'll prototype a small patch to kernel cost smoothing (moving average over last N choices) to avoid oscillation.
Devon: i will add the kv-pin test today and a repro script that toggles batch window vs kv-size.
Sophia: thanks. if anyone finds a single-commit repro on the PR branch let us know, then we can bisect faster.
Maria: update — CI for revert passed (job 6032110200) with median latency 12.0ms, p95 28.5ms. revert merged. rollout resumes.
Jon: great. leaving this thread open for the follow-ups (kernel smoothing PR, kernel selector logs, kv-pin tests).
Maria: creating follow-up task in tracker: PERF-1187 (investigate adaptive batcher -> kernel-route sensitivity).
Devon: assigning to Kevin + Sophia + Maria.
Sophia: tl;dr: small batching timing change caused kernel selection to pick fallback path more often, which indirectly increased KV evictions and pushed microbench over threshold. revert merged to unblock rollout.
Maria: :thumbsup: will post a short postmortem once we have the new instrumentation and a repro harness.
Jon: thanks team.
